evidence_items.publisher: International Journal of Social Research Methodology
evidence_items.locator: Discussion, page 6; transcription dates in Analyses, page 4
evidence_items.explanation: Whisper took about 8.5 hours against an extrapolated human baseline of 8.8 hours, providing modest support for faster transcription. Its generally usable transcriptions support preliminary-reference usefulness, although this is an inference from accuracy results rather than a direct quick-reference experiment.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract, Results; fieldwork dates in Methods
evidence_items.explanation: The March–June 2024 study of four translators reports an average 14% speed improvement when postediting GPT-4 translations instead of translating from scratch. Substantial editing and uneven individual gains qualify the benefit; the study nevertheless establishes a practical generative-AI translation gain before the post.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5, discussion of hiring and disability discrimination
evidence_items.explanation: The study documents fabricated speech and disproportionate hallucination risks associated with speech impairment. Its legal analysis identifies potential disability-discrimination exposure when such transcripts inform hiring, establishing a concrete risk mechanism rather than merely a generic accuracy concern.
